title: E-commerce transaction Poisson arrival stream and exponential interarrival gap
scenario_markdown: An e-commerce payment platform processes transactions arriving according to a Poisson process at an average rate of 12 transactions per hour. Management needs to calculate the probability that the interarrival time $X$ between consecutive transactions exceeds 10 minutes ($P(X > 10\text{ min})$).
assumptions: Poisson transaction arrivals at 12 per hour
Continuous interarrival time X ~ Exp(lambda = 12/60 = 0.20 per minute)
Mean time between transactions mu = 1/0.20 = 5 minutes
Duality P(X > t) = P(N_t = 0) holds between Poisson counts and exponential interarrival times

approval.notes: Verified rate lambda_min = 12/60 = 0.20 per min. P(X > 10 min) = exp(-0.20 * 10) = exp(-2) = 0.135335... Poisson count duality: mu_Y = 12 * (10/60) = 2.0. P(Y = 0) = exp(-2) * 2^0 / 0! = exp(-2) = 0.135335. Exact algebraic agreement.

stages.prompt_markdown: If transactions follow a Poisson process with arrival rate $\lambda = 12$ transactions per hour, what is the distribution and parameter of the continuous interarrival time $X$ (in minutes)?

options.text_markdown: $X \sim \text{Exp}(\lambda = 0.20\text{ min}^{-1})$ with mean interarrival time $\mu = \frac{1}{0.20} = 5$ minutes

options.hint_markdown: Interarrival time is a continuous variable measured on the real line, which follows the Exponential distribution, whereas Poisson models discrete counts of arrivals.

options.text_markdown: $X \sim \text{Exp}(\lambda = 12\text{ min}^{-1})$ with mean interarrival time $\mu = 12$ minutes
options.hint_markdown: Rate 12 per hour must be converted to minutes: $12/60 = 0.20$ transactions per minute.

stages.explanation_markdown: When event counts follow a Poisson process with hourly rate $\lambda_{\text{hr}} = 12$, the time between events follows an exponential distribution. Converting to minutes: $\lambda = 12/60 = 0.20$ transactions per minute, yielding mean gap $\mu = 1/0.20 = 5$ minutes.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate the probability that the gap between consecutive transactions exceeds 10 minutes: $P(X > 10) = e^{-0.20 \times 10} = e^{-2}$. Enter as a decimal rounded to at least three places (e.g., 0.135 or 0.1353).
stages.explanation_markdown: $P(X > 10) = e^{-2} \approx 0.1353$ (or $13.53\%$). Excel formula: `=1 - EXPON.DIST(10, 0.20, TRUE)` or `=EXP(-2)`.

stages.prompt_markdown: Why does the exponential survival probability $P(X > 10)$ exactly equal the discrete Poisson probability $P(Y = 0)$ for a 10-minute interval where expected arrivals $\mu_Y = 2.0$?

options.text_markdown: Waiting more than 10 minutes for the next arrival is logically equivalent to observing zero arrivals in that 10-minute span: $P(X > 10) = P(Y = 0) = e^{-2} \approx 0.1353$
It is only a numerical approximation that holds when $\lambda$ is small
options.hint_markdown: The relationship between Poisson counts and exponential interarrival times is an exact mathematical duality, not an approximation.
The complement of $X > 10$ is $X \le 10$, which corresponds to at least one arrival occurring ($Y \ge 1$).

stages.explanation_markdown: By definition, the interarrival time exceeds $t$ if and only if zero events occur in the time window $[0, t]$. In a 10-minute window, the expected count is $\mu_Y = 12 \times (10/60) = 2.0$. By Poisson PMF, $P(Y = 0) = \frac{e^{-2} 2^0}{0!} = e^{-2} \approx 0.1353$. In Excel, `=POISSON.DIST(0, 2, FALSE)` returns exactly `=1 - EXPON.DIST(10, 0.20, TRUE)`.
